note: Track sevenths-up, step 9: 13th chords, the 13 stacked on a 7th chord, tapped on the staff, the 7 and 9 pressed on the chord circle and all three named in the ear game ("qualities": 7, 9 and 13, its answers named as the buttons show them), then heard on the 5th chord over a backing track. The key is moves (any key): the old Key selector is gone, the chord is named as {{=key}}, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same. Missing: chord-circle has no 13th chord around its middle chord, so the 13 is only heard in the game and the backing track.

exercise.title: 13th chords: a 7th chord with the 13
exercise.why: A 13th chord is a 7th chord with the 6th above its root added an octave up, so the 13 is heard as one high note a 7th above the chord's ♭7.

cells.text:
{{=key}}13 is {{=key}}7 with one more note stacked on top. Tap {{1}}, {{3}}, {{5}} and {{b7}} from the lowest {{1}} on the staff below, then the ringed {{6}} that comes after the next {{1}}: that note is the 13th.
Then tap the first {{b7}} and that upper {{6}}, one after the other: those two notes are the sound of a 13th chord.
Practice until you can hum the 13th before you tap it.

The circle below has the chord on {{=key}} in the middle, the 5th chord of a major key. Press {{=key}}7 on the circle, then {{=key}}9.
Then press Start in the game under it: it plays a 7th, a 9th or a 13th chord from any root, and you pick Dominant 7, Dominant 9 or Dominant 13.
Practice until you can tell which high note each chord adds.

Press Play below to start the backing track: three chords, played twice. The second time, the 5th chord in the middle is a 13th chord and the other two stay as they were.
Look away from the chord boxes and call out "13" when the 13th chord comes.
Practice until you hear the high note the moment that chord starts.
{{?key}}In another key the chords have other names, and the 13th is still the 6th of the 5th chord, an octave up.
